newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai government defaults on rubber purchase.
newsitem.headline: Thai government defaults on rubber purchase.

text.p: Thailand will extend its government rubber intervention scheme by another three months but won't accept delivery of 23,100 tonnes of rubber bought from traders to cut losses, a senior minister said on Thursday.

Deputy Prime Minister Sukhawich Rangsitphol, who chairs the natural rubber policy committee, said the government expected to spend three billion baht in the next three months to prop up rubber prices in the domestic market.

He did not give further details on the defaults on the rubber purchase, but a government source said the decision was prompted by limited financial resources and an extremely bearish outlook for rubber prices.
The government earlier this year bought more than 40,000 tonnes of RSS3 rubber from traders in the FOB market for various delivery months to help prop up prices.
The delivery of the 23,100 tonnes batch was initially delayed on request by the government before it was cancelled.
It was purchased around at around 109.00 US cents a kg while the price of rubber has now fallen to 95-98 cents a kg.

On the price support scheme, Sukhavich said the government had adjusted the intervention prices to 27.50 baht a kg ($0.88) for grade-3 unsmoked sheet, 23.50 baht for grade 4 and 29.50 for smoked rubber sheet.
The new scheme will last until October, he said.
